name: Non-syndromic Syndactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Syndactyly

criteria.description: Presence of fusion between adjacent digits involving soft tissue or bone without other systemic anomalies
No associated craniofacial, neurological, or systemic abnormalities suggestive of syndromic forms
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of digit fusion without systemic anomalies and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist in confirming diagnosis and subtype classification

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers or toes
searchTerms: webbed fingers or toes fully connected
bones fused between finger or toe segments

common.symptomName: Partial webbing of digits with preserved distal separation
searchTerms: partial skin webbing between fingers or toes
digits partly joined but tips separate

common.symptomName: Reduced range of motion in affected digits
searchTerms: reduced flexibility in fingers or toes

common.symptomName: Asymmetrical involvement of hands and/or feet
searchTerms: one side affected more than other

common.symptomName: Mild digital deformity without functional impairment
searchTerms: mild finger or toe shape changes

occasional.symptomName: Nail plate abnormalities in fused digits
searchTerms: abnormal nail shape on joined digits
nail changes on fused fingers or toes

occasional.symptomName: Mild digital shortening of affected fingers or toes
Occasional mild functional limitation in fine motor skills
searchTerms: slight trouble with precise finger movements

rare.symptomName: Associated polydactyly in the same limb
searchTerms: extra finger or toe on same limb

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous syndactyly with minor pigmentation changes
searchTerms: webbed skin with slight color changes
skin color differences in fused digits

rare.symptomName: Transient mild swelling of fused digits
searchTerms: temporary mild swelling in joined digits
occasional puffiness of webbed fingers or toes

imaging: X-ray demonstrating soft tissue or bony fusion between adjacent phalanges
MRI to delineate extent of synostosis if needed
genetic: Mutations in genes such as HOXD13, FGFR2, and LMBR1 associated with various subtypes
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern commonly observed
other: Physical examination revealing webbing or fusion of digits without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic anomalies such as craniofacial dysmorphism
Localized absence of skin rather than digit fusion
Presence of scalp or limb skin defects

redFlags: Presence of craniofacial or systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic involvement
Progressive functional impairment of affected digits
Family history of syndromic malformations or genetic syndromes
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. Springer-Verlag; 1978.
